s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory distress with altered mental status and history of substance use
salient_findings: Unconsciousness with Glasgow Coma Scale of 3
Pneumothorax and severe emphysema with bullous changes on imaging
Positive urine drug screen for methamphetamines and opiates
key_facts: Required 15L oxygen on non-rebreather mask initially
Weaned to room air with normal oxygen saturation

Right lateral and basilar pneumothorax on initial chest radiograph

shortlist.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
shortlist.why_kept: History of 15 pack-year smoking and CT angiography showing severe emphysema and bullous changes

shortlist.label: Pneumothorax
shortlist.why_kept: Initial chest radiograph showing right lateral and basilar pneumothorax

shortlist.label: Emphysema
shortlist.why_kept: CT angiography showing severe emphysema and bullous changes throughout the lungs

shortlist.label: Bullous lung disease

shortlist.label: Opioid overdose

raw.rationale: The patient's CT angiography of the chest shows severe emphysema and bullous changes throughout the lungs, which is consistent with the patient's 15 pack-year smoking history and history of polysubstance use.

rejected.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of smoking, the primary diagnosis is more specifically emphysema, which is a component of COPD.

rejected.label: Pneumothorax
rejected.why: The patient did have a pneumothorax, but it is not the primary diagnosis that explains the patient's underlying condition.

rejected.label: Bullous lung disease
rejected.why: The patient's bullous changes are a part of the emphysema diagnosis, not a separate primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Opioid overdose
rejected.why: While the patient had a positive urine drug screen for opiates, the primary diagnosis that explains the patient's respiratory condition is emphysema.
